original_plan.expected_observation: A completed response search whose best replayed schedule is a full physical rollout with terminal error below 0.01 m, all six final-window position samples below 0.01 m and speeds below 0.02 m/s (a complete original-task pass), or at minimum a rollout improving the holding error from 0.0468 m by more than 2 cm together with the measured per-coefficient tip sensitivities, which reveal the plant static gain in the +z and -y directions.
original_plan.fixed_conditions: Frozen executable candidate b00bac (unchanged geometry, material, section, cells, tendon radius 0.023 m, viscosity 0.03, force limit 8 N, pretension 0.2 N); frozen task contract (target [0.29,-0.035,0.19] m, 0.01 m tolerance, 0.05 s holding window at 0.02 m/s, 0.35 s duration, 0.01 s control period); ideal-tension mode with [0,8] N bounds; baseline schedule is exactly the already measured constant [5.8047,4.5386,6.1808,1.6378] N; open loop only, no closed-loop controller, no evaluator or threshold change.
original_plan.hypothesis: The measured failure is a viscous, weak-drive creep, not a settled wrong posture: at t=0.30-0.35 s the tip velocity (-0.0017,-0.0102,+0.0214) m/s points directly at the target (need +0.033 m in z, -0.031 m in y) and the window speed is flat (0.02383 to 0.02372 m/s) with tip position moving only 1.2 mm, which is what a heavily damped system far from equilibrium looks like, not an approach to the local posture at z=0.157. x is already within 7.7 mm of the target. Therefore the residual is attributable to a net drive that is far too weak in the +z and -y directions: the applied differentials are only tendon_1-tendon_3 = 2.90 N and tendon_2-tendon_0 = 0.38 N, leaving roughly 5.1 N and 7.6 N of unused authority before the 8 N bound, and an early boost above the hold value should accelerate arrival so that the last 0.05 s is quiet. A two-knot open-loop schedule (early interval and hold interval) adjusted by measured finite-difference physical response should therefore either pass the frozen task or measurably shrink the residual.
original_plan.interpretation: If the search passes, the pass must be read at /acceptance and selected at once. If it improves without passing, the character of the improvement discriminates the two competing mechanisms without yet proving either: residual that shrinks with tension and then stalls at the bounds indicates the static target lies outside this candidate's reachable set (a design problem, addressable by softening the arm or enlarging the moment arm), whereas residual that shrinks while proposals remain interior indicates a timing/damping problem (addressable by lowering the candidate's bending viscosity or by a better-shaped schedule). The measured coefficient sensitivities are local information at one bend point only; they establish nothing about global feasibility, infeasibility, robustness, repeatability or hardware behaviour, and every pre-registered evaluator and threshold stays unchanged.
original_plan.stopping_condition: Stop immediately at the first complete passing original-task rollout: read /acceptance of that exact execution and select it. Otherwise stop once the search termination reason, its best replayed rollout with final-window error and speed, the per-coefficient tip sensitivities and the number of physical evaluations actually charged are known.
original_plan.weakening_observation: The search terminates without any replayed improvement (best holding error still near 0.047 m), or all proposals are invalid or numerically failed, or improvement stalls with the active coefficients pinned at the tension bounds while the residual still points outward, which would weaken the claim that the residual is a weak-drive artefact and would instead indicate the target lies outside this candidate's statically reachable set.
